links.outcome: Readability of radiology reports rated by 16 non-medical participants
links.effect: LLM-generated patient-centric reports significantly enhanced readability (P < 0.05); DeepSeek-R1 achieved the best performance
links.tradeoff: All models showed output instability, omitted information and risk-averse, generalized recommendations; patients' self-reported comprehension varied with demographic characteristics (age, education).
links.quote: Overall, large language models significantly enhanced the readability of radiology reports (P < 0.05), with DeepSeek-R1 achieving the best performance.

links.comparator_used: Baseline prompt (first stage of the two-stage prompt engineering strategy)
links.outcome: Output variance and translational accuracy of LLM-generated patient-centric reports
links.effect: Optimized structured prompts significantly reduced output variance and improved translational accuracy, most prominently in DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-4.0 (no numeric values given in the abstract)
links.quote: To address these limitations, optimized structured prompts significantly reduced model output variance and improved translational accuracy, with particularly prominent effects observed in DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-4.0.
